figures.title: Aster current-reading request and response
figures.Question: In what order do request, validation, response, and timeout occur?
figures.Reading: Controller sends ReadRequest, Sensor validates the request, then returns ReadingResponse; the dashed timeout path returns no reading.
figures.Limits: The view is fictional and omits transport encoding, authentication, and precise timeout duration.

purpose.content: The design explains the ordering for one current-reading request, including validation and timeout behavior rather than static schema details.

fields.design_subject: Synchronous request/validation/response flow between Controller and Sensor with one timeout alternate.
fields.requirements_links: Latest-reading query, explicit invalid-input rejection, and no-fabricated-value requirements drive the flow.

participants.content: Controller originates ReadRequest, Sensor checks sensorId and buffer state, and the operation boundary returns ReadingResponse or an explicit outcome.

fields.participants: Controller is the requester; Sensor is the provider; RingBuffer is an internal read-only participant, not an external actor.
fields.interfaces: ReadRequest carries sensorId; ReadingResponse carries Reading, NOT_READY, UNKNOWN_SENSOR, or TIMEOUT.

flow.content:
The numbered flow is request, validation, buffer read, then response; timeout cannot produce a ReadingResponse after the deadline.

![Aster request and response ordering](assets/interaction-flow.svg)

> **Figure D102-1 — Aster request and response ordering.**

> **Reading:** Controller sends ReadRequest, Sensor validates the request, then returns ReadingResponse; the dashed timeout path returns no reading.  
> **Limits:** The view is fictional and omits transport encoding, authentication, and precise timeout duration.

fields.interactions: Controller sends ReadRequest, Sensor validates sensorId, reads newest valid Reading, and sends ReadingResponse.
fields.ordering: Validation precedes buffer access, buffer access precedes response, and timeout terminates the attempt without a value response.
fields.diagram_decisions: [{"concern":"interaction-ordering","applies":true,"choice":"figure","rationale":"Numbered arrows and lifelines make request, validation, response, and timeout order explicit.","asset":"assets/interaction-flow.svg","model_view":"Example::InteractionFlow"}]

alternates.content: Unknown sensorId returns UNKNOWN_SENSOR before buffer access, empty history returns NOT_READY, and timeout produces no reading rather than a stale fabricated response.

fields.alternate_flows: UNKNOWN_SENSOR skips reading, NOT_READY follows an empty read, and TIMEOUT ends the operation without ReadingResponse.
fields.error_behavior: Errors are explicit outcomes and never mutate history or turn an old value into a newly timestamped reading.

constraints.content: The flow is read-only and single-request; concurrent retries, authentication, and transport retransmission are deliberately outside this example.

fields.behavior: One request produces at most one terminal outcome and never changes buffer contents or reading timestamps.
fields.constraints: No response after timeout, no buffer mutation, and no implicit retry or fallback value.

projection.content: Tests record event order for success, unknown sensor, empty history, and timeout paths and inspect the corresponding Example::InteractionFlow view.

fields.source_projection: RequestHandler, RequestValidator, ReadLatestExporter, and a controllable timeout are intended design units.
fields.verification_links: Ordered success, unknown-sensor, empty-history, and timeout event-sequence cases are planned checks.
